results.title: Playback Subscriptions | Explained
results.summary: Separates Playback Features (Intro, Premium, Cloud Pro, Live Bundle), Playback Content (Rentals, purchased tracks, Sounds, uploaded Cloud Songs, click and guide), and Playback Access (Team Sharing seats). Playback Intro is free on iOS, iPadOS, and macOS but limited to a single stereo output and excludes Premium features (editing arrangements, Playback Remote, Playback Sync). Cloud Pro adds click and guide for every song, Team Sharing seats, and saved custom-named arrangements; uploading Cloud Songs requires Cloud Pro. Rentals are device-specific and not shared. The article does not explain how to check or manage the subscription in-app.

results.title: GET STARTED | Cloud Pro Subscription
results.summary: What Cloud Pro gates for Playback: click and guide tracks for every catalog song in setlists (with key/tempo/arrangement edits persisting when tracks are later purchased or rented), saved Custom Arrangements (fader mix, key/tempo, sections), Cloud Songs with uploaded stems/charts/MIDI, custom click and guide cues, cloud-saved MIDI Cues, editing cloud sections, and 10 Playback Team Sharing licenses. Storage 'starts at 50GB' per this article (the pricing page lists other tiers). Cloud Pro also removes the 48-hour download expiration on purchased downloads. No activation or sign-in steps are given.

results.title: Playback User Guide
results.summary: The master user guide. Relevant documented points: the Audio Device setting (Settings > General > Audio Device) chooses the device Playback uses for all audio output; Auto Pan sends click/guide left and tracks right on the headphone output; MultiOuts (Premium) allow up to 32 outputs; track routing lives in Settings > Tracks and bus routing in Settings > Buses; purchased tracks download free; downloaded setlists stay on the device until removed or until a different user signs in; Settings > About has Manage Subscription and Restore Purchases.

steps.text: Select the output device: tap the stack icon (top-right) > Settings > General > Audio Device.

Auto Pan: Settings > General > Auto-Pan. Sends click and guide to the left output and all tracks to the right output of the device's stereo output, so you can run tracks from the headphone port without an interface.
Track routing: Settings > Tracks, tap an instrument part and choose a bus. Routing is device-specific and applies to that track across all songs and setlists on that device.
Bus routing: Settings > Buses, tap a bus cell, choose an output, tap Done. Swipe left on a bus to edit its name/abbreviation. Bus routing is saved per audio device.
If an output is greyed out it may be in use by SMPTE: change the SMPTE routing or disable SMPTE output in General settings.

Download a song: when adding a song, tap Add in the top-right corner. In the Setlists menu, tap Open Setlist, select a setlist, and tap the download icons to download tracks without loading the setlist, or load it to download every song automatically. Songs already on the device from another setlist show no download icon.

Remove one setlist from the device: open it in the Setlists menu and choose Remove Setlist From Device. Remove all: Setlists menu > Delete All Setlists From Device. This does not delete setlists from your MultiTracks.com account; re-download from the setlist menu to recover.
steps.caution: This removes the song from the device and re-downloads it, so only do it when you have time before you play.

steps.text: Subscription not recognized: Settings > About > Restore Purchases. The guide says: if an iTunes subscription is expired or not being confirmed by Playback, reconcile any payment issues in the App Store and tap Restore Purchases to reconnect your In-App Subscription.
steps.caution: Updating the app closes Playback and takes a few minutes; don't do this during a service.

steps.text: Side menu (stack icon) shows user name, organization name and ID, Switch Organizations, and Log Out.
steps.caution: Signing out can interrupt cloud access until you sign back in.

results.sectionPath: Playback User Guide > App Overview > Login Requirements > Organizational Content Permissions
results.text:
If you are logging into your own organization, then you are ready to start downloading your organization’s purchased content or Rental credits immediately. When logging into another organization, certain permission subscriptions need to be added to your account in order for you to access purchased tracks, spend Rental credits, or save Cloud changes to setlists, song arrangements, and MIDI Cues.

For more information about managing your organization’s team members, subscriptions, and content permissions, check out: 📖 Managing Roles and Permissions

Once logged in, you’re ready to start building a setlist!

results.sectionPath: Playback User Guide > Playback Settings > Side Menu: Settings & Features
results.text:
Playback's side menu has the following features:

- Main Settings Menu
- Waveform Size: adjustment
- Notifications: To toggle in-app notifications on or off.
- Playback Sync: To enable or disable Playback Sync broadcast from the Playback device.
- Playback Remote: The main Playback Remote menu to initiate a Playback Remote session, and/or connect a remote Playback device to a host Playback device. (📖Learn More)
- Network: the area to select which specific IP Address or network Playback Sync and Playback Remote broadcast through on host devices. (When utilizing multiple IP addresses or networks on a MacOS device).
- User Name, Organization Name, and Organization ID Number.
- Switch Organizations to switch between available organizations the signed-in user has access to.
- Log Out to log out the currently signed-in user of Playback.

Opening "Settings" in Playback's side menu will reveal the main Settings menu with the five settings' tabs; General, Tacks, Buses, MIDI, and About.
